test_intent: Verifies that AutoBanAsync sends the correct log notification type (AutoBanTextMention) when the reason string matches text mention patterns.
reason: Clean seam test at UserBanService level. Verifies notification type routing based on reason string. Mock verify is appropriate for this seam. No ID sensitivity issues.

test_intent: Verifies that AutoBanAsync sends the correct log notification type (AutoBanRepeatedViolations) when the reason string matches repeated violation patterns.
reason: Same pattern as text mention test. Validates notification routing for repeated violation reasons at the UserBanService seam. Clean mock verification.

test_intent: Verifies that AutoBanAsync falls back to the default notification type (AutoBanBlacklist) when the reason string does not match any known category.
reason: Tests the default/fallback notification routing path. Clean seam test at UserBanService level with appropriate mock verification.

test_intent: Should verify that AutoBanAsync bans the user and forwards their message, but only asserts the notification type was sent.
reason: Test name promises ban and forward verification but assertion only checks notification type, missing critical side effects like BanChatMember and message forwarding. The ban/delete side effects are the core bot contract worth preserving. Rewrite to also verify _botMock.Verify for BanChatMemberAsync and any message forwarding calls.

test_intent: Verifies that AutoBanChannelAsync handles exceptions gracefully by logging a warning and sending an error notification instead of crashing.
reason: Tests exception handling path in channel banning. Verifies error notification routing when Telegram API call fails. Mock choreography is appropriate for this seam. Medium maintenance risk due to exception simulation setup.

test_intent: Tests AI photo analysis by loading .env and calling the real external API to analyze a photo for attention bait.
reason: Test makes real external API calls and depends on .env file and local filesystem path (/home/kpblc/.../tmp/big.png), making it extremely fragile and non-portable. Assertions are weak (Not.Null, Length > 0) and do not validate AI analysis quality. Behavior (AI photo analysis) may be valuable but test is too expensive and flaky for CI. Quarantine until a proper mock-based or golden baseline replacement is designed.

test_intent: Verifies that the moderation flow processes a valid message and returns an Allow action with a reason.
reason: Test is misnamed as E2E but calls a mocked moderation service that returns a hardcoded Allow result, making the test a tautology. The 'correct order' claim is not tested at all. Assertions are basic (NotBeNull, Action == Allow, Reason not empty). The test does not exercise the actual integration flow. Rewrite as a proper unit test at the ModerationFacade seam if testing moderation decisions, or as a real integration test with the full pipeline wired through FakeTelegramClient.
